title: Logic Pro Crash Course
subtitle: 350+ Golden Nugget Tricks
tagline: No long tutorials. No fluff. Just what actually works.

pages.label: How to Use This Book
pages.title: How to Use This Book
body: Do not read this front to back. Jump to the section that matches what you are stuck on right now, take the trick, and get back to the music. Every section is one click away from every page.
Each entry is short on purpose. Title, what it does, the key command. Ten seconds to read, yours for good.
list: Every key command shown is the Logic Pro factory default on a US keyboard. If you have remapped anything, open Key Commands with ⌥K and search the command name — the name is always given.
Where a trick lives in a menu rather than on a key, the full menu path is written out, so it stays correct across versions.
Tricks marked GOLDEN NUGGET are the ones worth stealing first.
Tricks marked ADD YOUR NOTES are template slots for you to fill in.
Nothing here requires third-party plugins. It is all stock Logic.

callout.title: The one habit that matters most
callout.text: Every time you catch yourself doing something with the mouse for the third time, check whether it has a key command. If it does, learn it. If it does not, make one. That single habit is worth more than any individual trick in this book.

pages.label: Key Legend
pages.title: Key Legend
body: Logic's documentation and this book both use the Mac modifier symbols. If you are coming from another DAW, this is the page to bookmark.

keys.name: Option
keys.note: Almost always means copy, all, or alternate behaviour.

keys.name: Shift
keys.note: Extends a selection or reverses a command.

keys.name: Return
keys.note: Sends the playhead to the start of the project.

keys.name: Space
keys.note: Play / Stop. The most used key in the program.

callout.title: Three modifier rules that explain most of Logic
callout.text: Hold ⌥ while dragging anything and you copy it instead of moving it. Hold ⌥ while clicking any control and you reset it to its default. Hold ⌥ while clicking a button in a channel strip and the change applies to every channel at once. Learn these three and you can guess your way through most of the program.
